claims.statement: The GitHub OAuth flow always requests the scopes `repo,read:user,user:email` and uses plain OAuth 2.0 authorization code (no PKCE), with CSRF protection via `arctic`'s `generateState()` stored in a short-lived cookie.

Two environment variables back the GitHub OAuth app: `NEXT_PUBLIC_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` (client-exposed, used to build the authorize URL) and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` (server-only, used by the callback for the code exchange). Missing values are reported as `/?error=github_not_configured` from the sign-in routes and 500 from the callback.

The callback at `GET /api/auth/github/callback` dispatches between sign-in and connect by reading a `github_auth_mode` cookie whose value is either `signin` or `connect`. The mode cookie's presence also selects between the unified `github_auth_*` cookie names and the legacy `github_oauth_*` cookie names, so the callback tolerates flows started before the unified entrypoint existed.

In the sign-in flow the callback calls `createGitHubSession(accessToken, scope)` from `lib/session/create-github.ts`, which fetches the GitHub profile (with a `/user/emails` fallback when the public `email` is null) and runs `upsertUser({ provider: 'github', accessToken: encrypt(accessToken), refreshToken: undefined, ... })` so the encrypted token lands on the `users.accessToken` column. The resulting session is sealed with `encryptJWE(session, '1y')` via `saveSession`, after which the three `github_auth_*` cookies are deleted.

In the connect flow the callback encrypts the GitHub access token with `encrypt(token)` from `lib/crypto.ts` (AES-256-CBC, 16-byte random IV, 32-byte key from `ENCRYPTION_KEY`) before writing it to the `accounts.accessToken` column for the connecting internal user, with `refreshToken` always undefined because GitHub's standard OAuth flow does not issue one.

The connect branch in the callback handles three sub-cases after the code exchange: (1) same user reconnecting — update the existing `accounts` row's token in place; (2) conflict where the same GitHub numeric ID is already linked to a different internal user — reparent every row in `tasks`, `connectors`, `accounts`, and `keys` from the old user to the connecting user, delete the old `users` row, then update the `accounts` row; (3) fresh link — insert a new `accounts` row carrying the encrypted token.

`POST /api/auth/github/disconnect` deletes the linked `accounts` row for the current session and refuses (400) when `session.authProvider === 'github'` so the user is never left signed in with no underlying OAuth identity.

`GET /api/auth/github/status` returns `{ connected: false }` when there is no session, or `{ connected: true, username, connectedAt }` taken from either the `accounts` row (linked path) or the `users` row with `provider = 'github'` (primary path), so the UI shows the same "Connected as …" badge for both cases.

`getUserGitHubToken(req?)` in `lib/github/user-token.ts` is the canonical GitHub token reader: it resolves the session via `getSessionFromReq(req)` or `getServerSession()`, first looks up `accounts.accessToken` for the user with `provider = 'github'`, and falls back to `users.accessToken` for users whose primary identity is GitHub. It decrypts via `lib/crypto.ts`'s `decrypt` and returns the plaintext string (or `null`), and is consumed by the GitHub REST routes under `app/api/github/`, by the task creation and continuation routes, and by `lib/sandbox/agents/index.ts` to inject the user's GitHub token into the sandbox.

The callback clears the short-lived per-flow cookies after consuming them — the unified `github_auth_state` / `github_auth_redirect_to` / `github_auth_mode` set, the legacy `github_oauth_state` / `github_oauth_redirect_to` pair, and the connecting-user cookie `github_oauth_user_id` — and the unified sign-in entrypoint appends a `github_connected=true` query parameter to the post-auth redirect URL so the UI can show a one-shot toast after a successful connect.
